page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6r.large is a compute-optimized server instance built on the arm64 architecture, featuring dedicated Ampere Altra processors operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2 vCPUs, 4.0 GB of memory (providing 2.0 GB per vCPU), and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Virtualized using KVM without hyperthreading support, the architecture provides hardware-accelerated AES cryptography instructions, though it lacks x86-specific vector extensions and carries no local block storage.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average single-core CPU execution alongside lower multi-core and memory performance metrics. In synthetic stress-ng testing, the instance scored 1824.28 on single-core tasks and 3617.67 on multi-core tasks, with a PassMark CPU score of 1594.77. Uncached memory throughput reaches 26.08 GB/sec for reads and 16.11 GB/sec for writes in large block tests. Operational benchmarks record 2.83 million operations per second in Redis SET testing, 2.7 GB/sec static web serving throughput, and 58.25 tokens per second for text generation using a small 135M LLM model.

The hardware configuration provides dedicated ARM-based virtual cores suitable for entry-level deployments. Tradeoffs include the total absence of attached local disk storage and constrained memory throughput under larger block transfers. Given its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM profile and baseline network capabilities, this instance fits lightweight web serving, basic microservices, utility applications, and ARM software build environments that do not demand extensive memory bandwidth or local storage IOPS.

Synthetic evaluations indicate average single-core execution with a stress-ng single-core score of 1824.28, whereas multi-core and memory sub-systems show weaker metrics, including a PassMark CPU score of 1594.77 and 26.08 GB/sec uncached read memory bandwidth. Applied tests show throughput of 2.83 million Redis SET operations per second and 2.7 GB/sec in static web serving. The absence of local disk drives and moderate bandwidth characteristics position this instance as a lightweight entry for small microservices, utility tasks, basic web serving, and simple ARM development environments that prioritize dedicated vCPU resources over intensive memory performance or local storage.
